description: List the next passes of the ISS and other bright satellites over any latitude/longitude, computed with SGP4 from current orbital elements, ISS first. By default only passes visible to the naked eye (dark sky, satellite lit by the Sun). Use it for arbitrary coordinates; for a named European city with a calendar feed use iss_city_passes, to explain something already seen use what_did_i_see. Orbital elements come from the Vigi-Sky API (cached 10 minutes).

include_tle.description: Also return the two-line orbital elements used for the calculation (default false).

lang.description: Language of the text fields: fr (default) or en.

lat.description: Observer latitude in decimal degrees, WGS84 (north positive).

limit.description: Maximum number of passes to return (1-30, default 3).

lng.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees, WGS84 (east positive). lon and lng are aliases: give one.

lon.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees, WGS84 (east positive). lon and lng are aliases: give one.

night_only.description: true (default): only passes in a dark sky with the satellite sunlit. false: include daylight passes.

name: iss_passes

outputSchema.description: Returns passes [{name, start, max_el, az_start, az_max, az_end, end, potentially_visible}], night_only, citations, provenance.

title: Satellite passes over coordinates
